question.text: Mr. Arjun Mehta, promoter-sponsor of Garuda Credit Opportunities AIF (Cat II), wants to transfer his sponsor units to his personal HUF after 18 months to save tax. Which statement reflects the SEBI restriction?

answer.text: Sponsor units are freely transferable after a 1-year lock-in.
Sponsor can transfer to any related party provided SEBI is notified.
Sponsor units can be transferred only to accredited investors after 2 years.

The sponsor's continuing interest cannot be withdrawn and remains locked-in until distributions to investors are completed in full; any change of sponsor/manager or control requires prior SEBI notification/approval.

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that the sponsor's/manager's continuing interest cannot be withdrawn and remains locked-in until distributions to investors are completed in full. A transfer to a personal HUF is not a permitted exit from this lock-in. Separately, the workbook requires SEBI notification/prior approval for changes in manager/sponsor or change of control of an AIF. The Trap: Option A invents a 1-year freeze. Option B assumes notification alone cures the lock-in, ignoring that the continuing interest itself cannot be withdrawn. Option C mixes up accredited-investor rules with sponsor-unit transferability. Note: Two distinct rules apply — lock-in of continuing interest until full distribution, and SEBI approval for any change in sponsor/manager or control.
